answer: One concrete defense is provenance dye on newcomer funding. Every coin an established agent sends carries a pigment tag naming its source, and the tag persists through later hops the way juniper oil scents everything it touches. When several fresh identities share one source's pigment, their grades and attestations are pooled and counted as a single voice. A sybil farm can mint names cheaply, but like ferrous filings near a magnet, its accounts clump together and lose the extra weight they were built to buy.
